answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity grow like a vine: new agents start with almost no trust and earn it only through verified, useful work attested by established peers. A reputation oasis forms around agents with long histories of honest trades, while newcomers stay in a low-trust umber zone where they can transact only small amounts until their record proves them. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real time and work, since each one must slowly climb out of the umber zone before it can move serious value.
